Adjusted with the January 2017 Beige Book: activity expanded at a modest-to-moderate pace across most Districts, labor markets were tight with modest wage gains, and price pressures were modest—consistent with the FOMC’s “moderate” growth and sub-2% inflation characterization. However, the Beige Book also noted mixed consumer spending with plateauing auto sales and tighter auto underwriting, loan demand little changed, and some tightening or caution in CRE and construction—echoing SLOOS signals of neutral-to-slightly tighter credit outside prime mortgages. Manufacturing and energy showed modest improvement, while residential real estate remained a relative bright spot with low inventories and rising prices. Netting these, the credit channel and spending mix argue for maintaining a cautiously positive but slightly less upbeat tone than before, consistent with “gradual” policy normalization and roughly balanced near-term risks.
